exact_internal_explanations.text: The selected main text explicitly says four. Its daggered adjective ሠናያት means beautiful or fine (Dillmann1865 cols251–252), but Charles printed56 note12 regards it as corrupt and explains it through a Greek confusion involving hollows. This English retains the actual adjective in quotation marks rather than silently changing it to a hollow or compartment.

The parenthesized sentence, including I said, is printed in the selected main text but supplied by the editor from the Greek (Charles printed56 note15). Parentheses here preserve that editorial status; this is not an independently witnessed Ethiopic sentence.

The rolling expression is daggered as corrupt in the selected text (Charles printed56 note16). The root relates to rolling or causing to roll (Dillmann1865 col838, including Hen22:2); the short English rolling is only a qualified rendering of the damaged clause, not a restoration of its syntax or a claim that this means a cavern.

delivery: Internal anchors and exact notes retained. Reader renders marker-free prose and provides inconspicuous verse-click About this wording explanations. No visible footnote chrome required.
